sources.entry: AXe - CLI tool for controlling iOS Simulators through Accessibility APIs and HID automation. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/cameroncooke/AXe) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.one_liner: AXe is a command-line tool that automates iOS Simulators by driving Apple's HID input and Accessibility APIs, letting you inspect the UI, tap, type, and take screenshots from scripts or a terminal.
summary.what_it_does: AXe is a CLI for interacting with iOS Simulators through Apple's HID (Human Interface Device) functionality. The README shows commands to list simulators, describe the current UI, tap an element by its label, type text, and capture a screenshot, each targeted at a simulator UDID. It states support for Xcode 26 and Xcode 27, with Xcode 27 simulator automation going through Device Hub instead of Simulator.app. It builds IDB (Meta's iOS Development Bridge) from a pinned fork revision, and includes an end-to-end test runner that can validate release binaries under different Xcode versions. Full documentation is referenced at axe-cli.com/docs.
use_cases: automate taps and typing on iOS Simulator
script UI tests for iOS apps from the command line
inspect the accessibility tree of a running simulator
take screenshots of a simulator from a script
find simulator UDIDs and list available simulators
run automated simulator checks in CI pipelines
notable: Drives simulators via Apple HID and Accessibility APIs rather than requiring app-side instrumentation
Targets elements by accessibility label as well as coordinates
Supports Xcode 27 Device Hub workflow without needing Simulator.app
Release binaries can be validated unchanged across supported Xcode versions
Installable with a single Homebrew command
caveats: Requires Xcode 26 or 27; compatibility is validated only against the listed Xcode and iOS builds
Building end-to-end tests needs XcodeGen and a local IDB build
Built on Apple tooling, so it applies only to iOS Simulators on macOS
